title: PM daily scratchpad - 2026-03-22
content:
TODAY (2026-03-22)
- Morning focus: finalize PRD edits for v0.9 rollout notes + add rollout fallback table.
- Syncs: 10:00 eng sync (kernel selection), 11:30 design review (small UX change to streaming UI), 15:00 CS pre-brief for enterprise pilots.

Top priorities
1) PRD - v0.9 rollout (HIGH)
   - Action: incorporate SRE latency SLO wording + canary metrics.
   - TODO: add explicit fallback mapping: hosted -> dedicated -> private variants (see table draft below).
   - Note: need sign-off from Alex (SRE) and Priya (Product Ops) before EOD Weds.

2) Launch checklist for hosted-api streaming + function-calling beta
   - Verify streaming perf baselines (p90, p99) are in doc (ask infra for the latest run).
   - Confirm QA test plan covers partial-stream recovery + reconnect semantics.
   - Billing: confirm token accounting edge-cases with finance (Jordan).

3) Stakeholder follow-ups
   - Ping Alex about SRE sign-off (blocked if kernel perf regressions show).
   - Share PRD link to legal for retention wording by Thurs.
   - Update sales-facing one-pager (Leah) with final latency numbers and fallback story.

PRD edits (notes to self)
- Intro: reframe problem statement to emphasize production economics (latency + cost). Shorten background to 1 para.
- Add diagram: "routing policy flow" (hosted -> dedicated -> private). Placeholder image ref: confluence diagram id 8821.
- Table: fallback mapping for model variants + compatibility notes (model size, quantization, feature support).
- Metrics section: include p50/p90/p99, median cost per token, and canary thresholds. Add note: "Canary: 1% traffic for 24h, rollback if p99 latency > target or error rate > 0.5%".
- Risk: call out edge case for prefix-KV cache invalidation during rollout. Remedies: cache warming + traffic-weighted canary.

Quick launch checklist (working)
- [ ] PRD final draft linked in product folder
- [ ] SRE sign-off on canary metrics
- [ ] QA test plan + automated test jobs queued
- [ ] Billing/finance note added (token accounting)
- [ ] Support playbook drafted (error messages, escalation path)
- [ ] Sales one-pager updated
- [ ] Release notes + deprecation notes (if any) written

Meetings / talking points
- 10:00 eng: confirm kernel selection timeline and whether any perf regressions expected for longer contexts. Ask: how long to roll back? impact on rollback window.
- 11:30 design: streaming UX small change: move "stop streaming" CTA under response container (UX asked for microcopy tweak). Note: request updated mock today.
- 15:00 CS pre-brief: main ask = describe fallback behavior for enterprise customers and SLA implications. Provide sample incident runbook.

Blockers / open questions
- Kernel perf test results from infra still pending (status: infra running job, ETA 14:00).
- Legal review of data retention wording — need by Thu for launch.
- Billing edge-case: partial-stream tokens charged twice? Need confirmation from finance.

Decisions to capture (finalize before sign-off)
- Canary threshold definition: agree on p99 latency vs error-rate combined criterion.
- Streaming reconnect semantics: we will attempt 1 auto-reconnect for transient network failures; document client guidance.

Notes / scratch thoughts
- Consider adding "cost slider" in console to let teams trade-off batching vs latency (product idea, low priority).
- If kernel regressions show up for long-context models, consider temporary restriction: route >8k contexts to a conservative quantized variant.

Next actions (today)
- 09:30: update PRD with table + canary paragraph (me)
- 10:00: ask Alex about canary metrics (Jordan to sync if I’m in meetings)
- 11:45: follow up with design for updated mock
- 13:00: send draft support playbook to CS for review
- 16:30: compile final PRD + share to review group (Alex, Priya, Leah, Legal)

Misc links
- Draft PRD (product folder): confluence://PRD/v0.9-hosted-streaming (placeholder)
- JIRA: JIRA-API-4123 (rollout), JIRA-API-4150 (billing investigation)
- Slack threads: #hosted-apiops thread-4921 (kernel perf), #product-launch planning

Notes to self: keep language explicit about rollback criteria. Less marketing fluff in PRD — save that for the sales one-pager.

End of scratchpad
